why: The Old Testament poetry follows the Updated Brenton where Scrivener also sets the verse as poetry or has no say. Prose records verse-level exceptions following Scrivener. Its line boundaries are aligned to Brenton; breaks records the lines the words cannot place or would place wrongly. Boyd’s prose marker is retained at a poem’s end. Paragraphs records departures at existing prose boundaries: a continuation, repeated label, immediate response or closing action may remain flush left, while a new narrative or discourse unit keeps its paragraph. A change of speaker alone does not open a new unit. Each anchor is checked in the assembled, unrevised verse; joining changes paragraph structure alone.

prose.SIR 50:27: The author's colophon is prose in Scrivener's Cambridge Paragraph Bible; follow him here rather than Boyd's poetry.
